leaf_rust.what: A fungus that makes orange powdery spots under the leaves. Leaves fall early and the tree bears less next season.
check: Turn leaves over and look for orange powder on the underside.
Check whether many leaves have already fallen.
first_steps: Prune to open the canopy so leaves dry faster.
Remove fallen and badly infected leaves from the plot.
Keep trees well fed with manure or compost.
leaf_rust.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer before using any spray, and about rust-resistant varieties.

cercospora_nutrient_stress.what: Brown spots with a pale centre on leaves and berries. It is worse on trees that are hungry or in full sun.
check: Look for round brown spots with a light centre.
Check whether the worst trees are the ones with no shade.
first_steps: Add manure or compost around the trees.
Mulch to keep soil moist.
Consider planting shade trees in open areas.
cercospora_nutrient_stress.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer about a soil test and about feeding the trees.

leaf_miner.what: Small caterpillars that tunnel inside the leaf and leave brown blotches. Worse in dry seasons.
check: Hold a leaf to the light and look for brown blotches that peel like paper.
Check whether damage is mostly on the upper part of the tree.
first_steps: Keep some shade over the trees.
Mulch to reduce drought stress.
Encourage natural enemies by avoiding unnecessary sprays.
leaf_miner.contact_officer: Tell the extension officer if more than a few leaves on each tree are damaged.

phoma.what: A fungus that blackens young leaves and shoot tips in cold, wet and windy weather, mostly at higher altitudes.
check: Look for black, dying tips on new shoots.
Check whether damage is worst on the windy side of the plot.
first_steps: Plant or keep windbreaks.
Cut out and remove dead shoot tips.
Avoid pruning just before the cold wet season.
phoma.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer about protecting young shoots in the cold season.

berry_disease_suspected.what: Coffee berry disease makes dark sunken spots on green berries, which then rot or fall. The app cannot see berries, so this is only suspected.
check: Pick a few berries with dark spots.
Note how many trees are affected.
first_steps: Remove and bury infected berries away from the trees.
Prune to let air move through the canopy.
berry_disease_suspected.contact_officer: Take a sample of spotted berries to the extension officer to confirm.

berry_borer_suspected.what: A small beetle that bores a round hole in the berry and damages the bean. The app cannot see berries, so this is only suspected.
check: Look for a small round hole at the tip of the berry.
Open a berry and look for tunnels or small white grubs.
first_steps: Pick all ripe and overripe berries at harvest.
Collect and destroy berries that have fallen to the ground.
berry_borer_suspected.contact_officer: Take a sample of holed berries to the extension officer to confirm.

drought_stress.what: Too little rain during flowering or while berries grow means fewer flowers set and berries stay small.
check: Look for wilting in the afternoon.
Check whether flowers dried before setting berries.
first_steps: Mulch around the trees to keep soil moist.
Keep or plant shade trees.
Dig small basins or trenches to catch rain.
drought_stress.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer about water harvesting for your slope.

excess_rain.what: Heavy rain during flowering can wash out flowers and favour fungal diseases.
check: Check whether flowers fell before setting berries.
Look for water standing or soil washing away.
first_steps: Dig drainage channels along the slope.
Prune to let leaves dry faster.
Watch closely for berry and leaf diseases.
excess_rain.contact_officer: Tell the extension officer if you also see spots on berries or leaves.

soil_acidity.what: Very acidic soil makes it hard for coffee roots to take up nutrients, even when you add fertilizer. This comes from soil maps, not a test of your plot.
check: Ask whether your soil has ever been tested.
Check whether yellow leaves appear even after feeding.
first_steps: Get a soil test before changing anything.
Add well-rotted manure or compost.
soil_acidity.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer about a soil test and whether liming is needed.

nutrient_deficiency.what: Trees that are not fed enough bear less and are weaker against disease.
check: Look for pale or yellow leaves.
Think about when the trees were last fed.
first_steps: Add manure or compost around each tree.
Mulch with prunings and crop residue.
Plan feeding before the rains.
nutrient_deficiency.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer about a soil test and a feeding plan.

old_unpruned_trees.what: Old or crowded trees bear fewer berries on less new wood. Pruning renews bearing branches.
check: Count how many main stems each tree has.
Look for long bare branches that bear only at the tips.
first_steps: Remove dead, crossing and low branches.
Plan to renew the oldest trees a few at a time.
old_unpruned_trees.contact_officer: Ask the extension officer to show the pruning method for your variety.
